title: Drop What the Model Disagrees With: Out-of-Fold Filtering for Label Noise
storyline: A linear classifier trained on wrong labels loses accuracy. A known remedy, classification filtering, drops training samples that held-out predictions contradict. The paper claims no new method; it measures what one single-learner out-of-fold filter (logistic regression for both the check and the refit) removes, recovers and costs on two small datasets with clean and symmetrically noisy labels, checking every drop against the injected flips. Under noise most drops are mislabeled and the kept set holds a far smaller mislabeled share than the training set, although correct samples are discarded and removal overshoots the flipped share. The refit model has a higher mean accuracy than logistic regression with the same settings in every noisy setting (not significant on breast cancer at the lower rate) but stays below the clean-label reference in all of them, with little recovery on breast cancer at the higher rate. With clean labels it removes few samples and costs little. Revised after review round 0.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.goal: The reader knows in one paragraph what the filter asks for (only the noisy training set), what it does in one pass, and what it achieved on two small datasets, including where it falls short.
points: Problem and known remedy: label noise lowers the accuracy of linear classifiers; dropping samples that held-out predictions contradict is a known remedy, which we measure.
The filter in one sentence, with what it does not use (clean set, noise rate, threshold).
Breadth: digits and breast cancer, clean labels and two symmetric noise rates.

Main findings: most drops mislabeled and a much cleaner kept set; mean accuracy above logistic regression with the same settings in every noisy setting (not significant on breast cancer at the lower rate); only partial recovery, least on breast cancer at the higher rate; mean below clean-label training in every noisy setting; little cost on clean labels. No numbers; the MLP is not mentioned.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.goal: The reader knows the question (what one linear out-of-fold filter removes, recovers and costs on small clean and symmetrically noisy training sets), sees the filter and the measured answer in Fig. 1, and knows the three contributions and their scope.
points: Problem: cheaply gathered labels contain errors; symmetric label noise lowers the test accuracy of logistic regression on both datasets, more at the higher rate (gray marks in Fig. 1c).

Question, with Fig. 1a: what does one linear out-of-fold filter remove, recover and cost? Describe the filter in two sentences; a plain instance of classification filtering and a relative of confident learning; no new method claimed.
Central finding, italic once: on these two datasets, most samples the filter drops under noise are mislabeled, yet refitting wins back only part of the lost accuracy.

Three contributions: (1) a measurement of a known filter; (2) what it removes; (3) mean accuracy between logistic regression with the same settings and the clean-label reference (not significant on breast cancer at the lower rate), little cost on clean labels.

sections.title: Related Work
sections.goal: The reader knows what the closest antecedent reported, places the filter among other ways to handle noisy labels, and knows what this study measures rather than any claim of novelty or superiority.
points: \paragraph{Filtering mislabeled samples.} What Brodley and Friedl report in their abstract (single-algorithm, majority and consensus filters on five datasets, accuracy gains up to a stated noise level, the trade-off between discarding good data and keeping bad data); confident learning; other data filters. Then what this study reports: mislabeled share left in the kept set, drops on clean and noisy labels, share of lost accuracy won back. Claim no omission that the abstract does not settle.
\paragraph{Sample selection for deep networks.} Co-teaching and per-sample-loss methods select during training; our filter selects once.

\paragraph{Noise models and noise-tolerant training.} Surveys; loss correction, reweighting and noise-tolerant logistic regression keep the samples; we change the training set and test only symmetric noise. No numbers.

sections.title: Filtering Labels with Out-of-Fold Predictions
sections.goal: The reader can implement the filter from this section and understands why an out-of-fold prediction is a fair check on a label: the model that judges a sample never saw it.
points: \paragraph{Setting.} Start from the baseline it changes. A training set of n samples with features and given labels, some of which may be wrong. Define the base model once as a function: f_D, standardization followed by logistic regression fit on a set D, maps a feature vector to a class. Plain logistic regression is f_D on all given labels. Notation is defined once and used consistently.
\paragraph{Out-of-fold check.} Split the training set into K folds stratified on the given labels. Each sample receives the hard prediction of f fit on the K-1 folds that exclude it.

\paragraph{Keep rule and refit.} Introduce in words, then one equation: the kept set is every sample whose out-of-fold prediction equals its given label; the final model is a fresh f (scaler refit too) on the kept set. Refer to Fig. 1a.
\paragraph{What it does not need.} No clean validation set or noise-rate estimate, as one property of the design. Only K and the regularization strength are fixed.

sections.title: Experiments
sections.goal: Opens the Experiments section with a compact setup. The reader knows the data and how symmetric noise differs between a two-class and a multi-class task, what isolates filtering, what is measured and when a difference counts as established.
points: \paragraph{Data and noise.} Digits (multi-class handwritten digits) and breast cancer (two-class diagnosis, benign or malignant), split sizes; stratified split with the test fraction, shared across noise rates; symmetric noise at two rates, flips nested across rates. Print no class counts.

\paragraph{Methods.} The only comparison that isolates filtering is logistic regression with the same fixed C; no other noise treatment was run. The MLP asks whether a larger model on the same labels makes filtering unnecessary.
\paragraph{Settings.} scikit-learn defaults (versions not recorded), iteration limits, MLP size.

\paragraph{Measures.} Accuracy; removed share, drop precision and recall, mislabeled share of the kept set, share of correct samples dropped (per seed, then averaged); share of lost accuracy won back as a displayed ratio of seed means.

\paragraph{Statistics.} Keep the Scriptorium sentence. Established: two-sided paired t-test over seeds at the five percent level, no multiplicity correction; overlapping splits make p-values likely too low.

sections.title: Under noise, the filter leaves a much cleaner training set
sections.goal: Subsection of Experiments. The reader believes that the filter leaves a far cleaner training set than random removal would, while discarding correct samples, and that heavier noise costs it on both sides.
points: Removal grows with noise and exceeds the flipped share in every noisy setting; small on clean labels (two numbers).

Random removal would leave the mislabeled share unchanged, with precision equal to the flipped share and recall equal to the removed share; the filter does much better. Most drops are mislabeled in every noisy run (per-run range).
At the higher rate, on seed means, the filter misses more flips and discards more correct samples; compare precision only with the flipped share. Attribute no accuracy gain to these quantities.

sections.title: Refitting wins back part of the accuracy lost to noise
sections.goal: Subsection of Experiments. One finding per paragraph: the mean gain over logistic regression with the same settings, the gap to the clean-label reference, how recovery differs by setting, the weak case, and the MLP.
points: Higher mean than logistic regression with the same settings in every noisy setting, ahead in all noisy runs but one; not established on breast cancer at the lower rate (p-value); no random-drop or oracle control, so no attribution to removing the right samples.
Mean below the clean-label reference in all four noisy settings; both lower-rate gaps borderline (p-values); all four gap verdicts tentative.
Much returns on digits at both rates and, with an unresolved gain and unstable per-seed share (range), on breast cancer at the lower rate.
Weak case: on breast cancer at the higher rate, the two least accurate seeds have the most flips and the largest mislabeled share left (association over five seeds).
Two sentences: the MLP does not make filtering unnecessary; logistic regression also beats it, so the gap says nothing about filtering.

sections.title: On clean labels, the filter costs little
sections.goal: Subsection of Experiments. The reader sees the size of the clean-label cost: a small per-seed range on digits, one test sample in one seed on breast cancer.
points: Cost by its scale: per-seed range of the paired difference on digits; on breast cancer the models differ in one seed only, by one test sample; neither mean difference established, no equivalence claimed.

sections.title: Discussion and Limitations
sections.goal: The reader leaves knowing what one fixed filter did in the tested settings, what it did not restore, and what remains open.
points: The filter ran without being told the noise rate or whether labels were noisy, and left a cleaner set under noise; mean below the clean-label reference in all noisy settings; correct samples discarded.

Limitations as next steps: two small datasets, symmetric noise at two rates, one pass with fixed K and C, one untuned MLP not combined with the filter; tested only where clean-label logistic regression is very accurate; regularization confound at fixed C; no random-drop, oracle or in-sample controls; no co-teaching or confident learning.

Columns grouped by dataset (digits, breast cancer), each clean, 20% noise, 40% noise. Bold the best mean in each column, ties included. Caption: logistic regression at clean labels is the clean-label reference; test sizes per split; booktabs, one decimal throughout.

Table 1, single column, noisy settings only so no cell is empty. Columns grouped by dataset: digits 20% and 40%, breast cancer 20% and 40%. Rows: flipped share of the training set; mislabeled share of the kept set; share of the training set removed; drop precision; drop recall; share of correctly labeled samples dropped; share of lost accuracy won back. All in %, means over 5 seeds. The caption gives the flipped-share ranges of the two least accurate seeds and of the other three on breast cancer at 40%.

figures.message: One out-of-fold pass drops mostly mislabeled samples under noise and few samples on clean labels; the refit model gains over logistic regression with the same settings on average but its mean stays short of the clean-label reference.
figures.spec: Full-width figure with three panels, plain sans-serif labels, no equations. Panel (a) 'Filter noisy labels': schematic of the noisy training set (a wrong label and the correctly labeled sample that is later dropped are marked; pills 'Needs no clean set' and 'Needs no noise rate') and four numbered stages: predict out of fold, compare, drop, refit once. Panel (b) 'What it removes': stacked bars of the share of the training set removed in the six settings, split into mislabeled and correctly labeled, with black ticks for the share mislabeled in the training set. Panel (c) 'What it gains and costs': bars of ours minus logistic regression test accuracy (points, paired per seed) from a true zero, sd error bars and seed dots, clean columns included; zero line in the partner color labeled logistic regression; a gray mark per noisy setting at the clean-label reference on the same scale. Legends above panels; colors by role from scriptorium_diagram and scriptorium_fig.
figures.caption: What the out-of-fold filter does, what it removes and what it gains. Read each panel and give one takeaway per panel.

related.topic: Classification filtering of mislabeled training data
related.why: Our filter is a single-algorithm member of this family: drop training samples that a held-out classifier misclassifies. We present it as such and claim no new method.
